definitions.explanation: A small smelt-like fish grilled and eaten whole, head and all, a staple of izakaya menus. The true shishamo lives only off Hokkaido; most of what is sold under the name is imported capelin.

examples.japanese: シシャモ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
⟦{子持|こも}ち→子持ち：12303_komochi⟧シシャモ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{居酒屋|いざかや}→居酒屋：09635_izakaya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{定番|ていばん}→定番：12265_teiban⟧だ。
examples.english: Shishamo full of roe is an izakaya standard.

examples.japanese: ⟦{店|みせ}→店：00497_mise⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{売|う}られている→売る：00906_uru⟧シシャモ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{多|おお}く⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{実|じつ}→実：28344_jitsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{輸入|ゆにゅう}→輸入：01742_yunyuu⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧カラフトシシャモだ。
examples.english: Most of the shishamo sold in stores is actually imported capelin.

notes:
The word comes from Ainu. The kanji spelling {柳葉魚|ししゃも} ("willow-leaf fish") is a reading assigned to the whole word.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{子持|こも}ち→子持ち：12303_komochi⟧シシャモ: shishamo with roe, the most prized
- シシャモ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧: to grill shishamo
- {本|ほん}シシャモ: true Hokkaido shishamo, as against カラフトシシャモ (capelin)
